reported.title: is_bipartite_dfs ignores recursive result

reported.claim: set(start) builds a set of the characters of the start string rather than a set containing the start vertex, so multi-character vertex names are wrongly split into their characters.
reported.title: depth_first_search set(start) splits multi-character vertex names

reported.claim: The loop removes items from self.graph[u] while iterating over it, so after one removal the next matching parallel edge is skipped and survives, although the docstring says all edges u->v are removed.
reported.failing_call: g = DirectedGraph(); g.add_pair(0, 5, 2); g.add_pair(0, 5, 3); g.remove_pair(0, 5); g.graph[0]
reported.title: DirectedGraph.remove_pair mutates list while iterating

reported.claim: Removing from self.graph[u] while iterating over it skips the element after each removed match, so parallel edges to v are not all removed.
reported.failing_call: g = Graph(); g.add_pair(0, 5, 2); g.add_pair(0, 5, 3); g.remove_pair(0, 5); g.graph[0]
reported.title: Graph.remove_pair mutates list while iterating

reported.claim: When exactly two nodes have odd degree the function falls through to return 3 instead of returning 2 (Euler path), so the path case is never detected.
reported.title: check_circuit_or_path never returns 2 for Euler path

reported.claim: The function returns the integer n instead of the donor-to-recipient matching stored in donor_record.
reported.title: stable_matching returns n instead of matching

reported.claim: The first cell of each row subtracts the cell above instead of adding it, so the path sum for the first column is wrong.
reported.title: fill_row subtracts cell above in first column

reported.claim: When the capacity is positive but smaller than the best-ratio item's weight, k is 0 and the function returns 0 instead of a fraction of that first item.
reported.title: frac_knapsack returns 0 when capacity is less than first item's weight

reported.claim: The word slice is `block[i : i + 32 - 1]`, which takes 31 bits instead of 32, so `to_little_endian` raises ValueError on every block.
reported.expected: A list containing one block of 16 integer words (no exception).
reported.title: md5 get_block_words slices 31 bits instead of 32

reported.claim: The recursive branch subtracts weights[counter + 1] instead of the weight of the current item, weights[counter - 1], which gives the wrong capacity and raises IndexError on the last item.
reported.title: knapsack_recur uses wrong item weight index

reported.claim: The off-diagonal sum uses signed subtraction instead of the absolute values, so matrices that are not diagonally dominant pass the check and no ValueError is raised.
reported.expected: ValueError to be raised (diagonal 1 does not exceed the off-diagonal sum 5)
reported.title: strictly_diagonally_dominant omits absolute values

reported.claim: The top-left and bottom-right entries use 2*c - 1 and 2*s - 1, but a reflection matrix for a line at angle θ needs 2*c*c - 1 and 2*s*s - 1 (the same formula as projection, scaled), so the result is not a reflection.
reported.title: reflection matrix uses 2*c-1 and 2*s-1 instead of squared terms

reported.claim: The function returns the leftover loop variable item_tuple instead of the accumulated pruned list, so callers get a tuple (or an UnboundLocalError when there are no candidates) rather than the filtered candidates.
reported.title: prune returns leftover loop variable instead of list

reported.claim: inc subtracts num_occur from the count instead of adding it, so repeated transactions reduce node counts rather than increase them.
reported.expected: The node's count should become 5 (inc returns None, so check the count attribute: TreeNode('A', 2, None) after inc(3) has count 5).
reported.title: TreeNode.inc subtracts instead of adds

reported.claim: The label range check uses '>' instead of '>=', so a label equal to vocab_size passes validation and then indexes past the end of the one-hot eye matrix.
reported.expected: ValueError (label 3 is out of range for vocab_size 3)
reported.title: perplexity_loss label check allows label equal to vocab_size

reported.claim: The epsilon is subtracted inside the square root instead of added, as the module docstring's update rule sqrt(v(t) + epsilon) requires, so zero moving averages make math.sqrt receive a negative number and crash.
reported.title: rmsprop subtracts epsilon instead of adding

reported.claim: The function returns side2 instead of the computed Heron's formula area.
reported.title: area_triangle_three_sides returns side2

reported.claim: The trial-division loop stops at sqrt(n) and never multiplies in a leftover prime factor greater than 1, so the sum of divisors is missing that prime's (p+1) contribution.
reported.title: sum_of_divisors omits leftover prime factor

reported.claim: The origin latitude is read from origin[-1] (the longitude) instead of origin[0].
reported.title: initial_bearing reads origin latitude from longitude

reported.claim: The loop condition x < b - h excludes the last interior point b - h, so that point's Simpson weight is dropped whenever float rounding does not happen to keep it in range, giving a wrong integral for larger step counts.
reported.title: make_points excludes last interior point

reported.claim: The loop ends with prev_num holding P_n, but the function returns prev_prev_num, which holds P_(n-1), so every n >= 2 gives the wrong value.
reported.title: pell_number_iterative returns wrong term

reported.claim: The accumulator starts at 1 instead of 0, so the sum is inflated by 1 and the mean is wrong for every non-empty list.
reported.title: arithmetic_mean accumulator starts at 1

reported.claim: The base case B_0 = 1 is written to the last index (bell[-1]) instead of bell[0], so bell[0] stays 0 and every later Bell number is wrong.
reported.title: bell_numbers writes B_0 to bell[-1]

reported.claim: The split loop stops at digits - 2, so it never tries the split that leaves a single leading digit on the left; valid Kaprekar numbers such as 9 (81 = 8 + 1) are rejected.
reported.title: is_kaprekar split loop misses single-digit left split

reported.claim: The search starts at index 1, so row 0 is never examined and values in the first row are reported as not found.
reported.title: mat_bin_search skips row 0

reported.claim: The empty-input guard uses 'matrix_b' instead of 'not matrix_b', so any non-empty pair of matrices returns an empty list.
reported.title: kronecker_product empty guard wrong, returns empty for valid input

reported.claim: `next_row = current_row` aliases the two rows, so the diagonal and bottom lookups read values already overwritten in the current row, giving squares that include zeros.
reported.title: largest_square_area bottom-up space-optimized aliases rows

reported.claim: The size check requires both operands to have identical shapes, which rejects valid products such as a 3x2 matrix times a 2x2 matrix, so multiply fails on inputs it should handle.
reported.title: _verify_matrix_sizes requires identical shapes for multiply

reported.claim: leap_day_reinstall_number uses true division, producing a fractional value for years where year//100 is not a multiple of 4, which corrupts the day offsets and gives the wrong date.
reported.title: gauss_easter leap_day_reinstall_number uses true division

reported.claim: The loop upper bound `len(sorted_points) - 1` skips the last sorted point, so it can never be added to the hull.
reported.title: graham_scan loop skips last sorted point

reported.claim: The swap rewires pointers incorrectly: previous_node.next is set to the predecessor instead of node, and the node's old next is lost, corrupting the list when a node moves forward.
reported.failing_call: (lambda d: (setattr(d.add.__self__, 'x', 0), d))(DoubleLinkedList()) and then: dll = DoubleLinkedList(); a = DoubleLinkedListNode(1, 1); a.freq = 5; dll.add(a); b = DoubleLinkedListNode(2, 2); dll.add(b); dll.head.next.key
reported.title: _position_node swap rewires pointers incorrectly

reported.claim: The formula is inverted: from r1/r2 = sqrt(m2/m1) one gets m2 = m1 * (r1/r2)^2, but the code computes (r1/r2)^2 / m1.
reported.expected: 7.880... (2 * (1.408943/0.709752)^2 ≈ 7.88), not the value 1.970351 that the doctest currently records
reported.title: second_molar_mass formula inverted

reported.claim: The check `tangential_force <= 0` rejects a tangential force of exactly zero, which is a valid unknown-value input, so the `tangential_force == 0` branch can never run.
reported.title: shear_stress rejects zero tangential force

reported.claim: The slot check uses the task's position among all sorted tasks, including rejected ones, instead of the number of tasks already accepted, so a rejected task wrongly pushes later tasks past their deadlines.
reported.title: max_tasks slot check uses position among all tasks

reported.claim: When the CPU is idle before a process arrives, the clock should jump to the arrival time, but `+=` adds the arrival time to the current time instead of setting it.
reported.title: first_come_first_served idle clock advanced with += instead of set

reported.claim: When the CPU is idle before a process arrives, the clock is advanced by the arrival time with `+=` rather than set to it, so completion times are wrong.
reported.title: round_robin idle clock advanced with += instead of set

reported.claim: The loop passes the whole tail arr[i:] to median_of_five instead of the five-element group arr[i:i+5], so the medians are taken over up to len(arr) elements rather than groups of five.
reported.title: median_of_medians passes whole tail instead of group of five

reported.claim: The n <= 1 guard only executes 'pass', so for an empty list block_size becomes 0 and range(0, n, 0) raises ValueError instead of returning an empty list.
reported.title: kirkpatrick_reisch_sort n <= 1 guard does nothing, empty list raises

reported.claim: The loop runs over len(sorted_list_2d) + 1 indices, but sorted_list_2d has only len(sorted_list_2d) pairs, so the final iteration indexes past the end and raises IndexError for any input with at least one pair.
reported.title: merge_insertion_sort loop indexes past end

reported.claim: The zeros group is recursed with bit_position + 1 instead of bit_position - 1, so it moves away from the bit being examined and never terminates for duplicate values, causing a RecursionError.
reported.title: _msd_radix_sort recurses zeros group with bit_position + 1

reported.claim: The swap test compares collection[i - 1] with collection[i] but then swaps collection[i] and collection[i + 1], so the pair being compared is not the pair being swapped and the list is left unsorted.
reported.title: odd_even_transposition compares one pair but swaps another

reported.claim: The `or` lets any 13-digit number pass without checking the check digit; the docstring says it checks both length and last digit, so this should be `and`.
reported.title: is_valid barcode uses 'or', skipping check digit

reported.claim: The guard `m >= len(text)` returns -1 when the pattern is exactly as long as the text, so a text that equals the pattern is never matched.
reported.title: bitap_string_match fails when pattern length equals text length

reported.claim: When the weighted sum is divisible by 10 the check digit should be 0, but `10 - subtotal % 10` yields 10, so a valid PESEL with check digit 0 is rejected.
reported.title: is_polish_national_id rejects check digit 0

reported.claim: The swap guard uses `<=` instead of `<`, so two words of equal length swap and recurse forever, raising RecursionError instead of returning the distance.
reported.title: levenshtein_distance_optimized swaps equal-length words forever

reported.claim: The function returns the loop variable `word` (the last word split from the sentence) instead of the `occurrence` dictionary it builds.
reported.title: word_occurrence returns last word instead of dictionary
